item.title: On the Classification of Nilpotent Lie Superalgebras over Fields of Characteristic 2
item.description: arXiv:2611.14523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The salient result of this paper is the complete classification of all nilpotent Lie superalgebras in dimensions up to four over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2. Our method adapts the Skjelbred-Sund method to show that every n-dimensional nilpotent Lie superalgebra arises as a one-dimensional central extension of an (n-1)-dimensional one, and determines precisely when two such extensions yield isomorphic superalgebras. Carrying out this construction for dimensions up to 4, we obtain a finite, non-redundant list of pairwise non-isomorphic examples.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Uzair Haroon

item.title: Quivers with potential for quantum affine superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a surjective algebra homomorphism from the $K$-theoretic Hall algebras of certain quivers with potential to the (half) quantum affine and toroidal orthosymplectic superalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Negu\c{t}

item.title: Incidence Geometry of Local Maxima: Howe Duality and Branching
item.description: arXiv:2611.14591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite or compact group, consider the mean squared matrix coefficient on the unit sphere. Its local maxima are the vectors generating irreducible cyclic subrepresentations. We show that for compatible group actions this variational picture retains the incidence structure of representation theory. For two commuting actions, intersections of projectivized local-maximal components recover the weighted support graph of the product representation, including its multiplicity spaces; Howe duality is the multiplicity-one matching case. More generally, for pairwise commuting actions, and for subgroup chains, every positive linear combination of the corresponding functionals has exactly their common local maxima, while every other critical point has a positive Hessian direction. On a fixed irreducible module at the top of a subgroup chain, the simultaneous projective local-maximal components are indexed by vertex paths in the weighted Bratteli diagram. Each component is the product of the projective space of the bottom representation and the projectivized branching multiplicity spaces. In the multiplicity-free case with one-dimensional bottom type, these reduce to the Gelfand-Tsetlin lines. Peter-Weyl, Frobenius reciprocity, Young branching and Schur-Weyl duality provide concrete instances of the general picture.
item.dc:creator: Pin-Chi Hung, Ming-Hsuan Kang

item.title: Sign components for general bosonic-fermionic coinvariant rings
item.description:
arXiv:2611.14773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the sign-isotypic components of the symmetric group coinvariant rings $R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(a,b)}$ and $R_n^{(k+a,\ell+b)}$ are isomorphic if and only if $n \leq 2$ or at least one of $(k,\ell)$ or $(a,b)$ is $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$. Moreover, for $k \geq 1$ the $
u$-isotypic components $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_n^{(0,1)}ight)^
u$ and $\left(R_n^{(k,\ell+1)}ight)^
u$ are isomorphic if and only if $
u$ corresponds to the sign representation. We also show that the socle of $R_n^{(k,\ell)}$ always contains the sign component, extending one direction of a result of Haiman for $R_n^{(2,0)}$. We settle the hook components conjecture of Bergeron (2024) for coinvariant rings, and a conjecture of Bergeron (2020) that the multiplicity of the sign character of $R_n^{(1,2)}$ is $3^{n-1}$. Our results also recover several existing results in the literature. Lastly, we extend our results to the hyperoctahedral group ${\mathfrak{B}_n}$ and prove that the determinant-isotypic components of $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell)} \otimes R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(0,1)}$ and $R_{\mathfrak{B}_n}^{(k,\ell+1)}$ are isomorphic.
item.dc:creator: Nicolle Gonz\'alez, John Lentfer, Pablo S. Ocal

item.title: Maximal nilpotence for higher Verlinde categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.14810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that all higher Verlinde categories are maximally nilpotent, as conjectured by Coulembier (2023). By previous results, it suffices to show that non-trivial simple objects have only finitely many non-zero symmetric powers in odd characteristic. We compute the maximal degrees of these non-zero symmetric and exterior powers explicitly, hence confirming their finiteness. We discuss some of the far-reaching consequences.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Johannes Flake, Joseph Newton, Victor Ostrik

item.title: Cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study cluster-roots of $n$-representation-finite algebras, namely the dimension vectors of cluster-indecomposable modules. We give a direct proof of Mizuno's higher analogue of Gabriel's theorem, and show that cluster-roots are precisely the non-negative integer vectors whose Coxeter orbits contain the dimension vector of an indecomposable projective module. Moreover, we give an explicit description of all cluster-roots of the $(n-1)$-Auslander algebras of type $A$. For $n=2$, we use periodic integer sequences to give a method for constructing counterexamples to Mizuno's positivity conjecture within this family, which reduces to determining whether finitely many quadratic equations admit non-negative integer solutions.
item.dc:creator: Weikang Weng

item.title: Inhomogeneous First-order Differential Operator Representations of $E_6$ and Graded Betti Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.15245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize the restricted dual Verma modules of arbitrary highest weight for the complex simple Lie algebra of type $E_6$ by inhomogeneous first-order differential operators in $36$ variables. The construction is obtained by applying Xu's functor (2016) to the full conformal oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{o}(10)$. We construct polynomial bases for all six fundamental $E_6$-modules and obtain a finite spanning set for every finite-dimensional irreducible $E_6$-module $V(\lambda)$. The degree in $16$ selected variables gives $V(\lambda)$ a grading over the symmetric algebra of the opposite abelian nilradical. We compute its Hilbert series and graded Betti numbers, and verify the Buchsbaum-Eisenbud-Horrocks conjecture for this family. The minimal graded free resolution of $V(\lambda)$ is pure precisely when $\lambda$ is a nonnegative multiple of the Weyl vector of $E_6$. Among nonzero dominant integral $\lambda$'s, the minimum total Betti number is $435204$, attained exactly at two minuscule weights $\omega_1$ and $\omega_6$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Zhou

item.title: $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.15332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all controlled $2$-blocks with defect group of rank $2$ up to Morita equivalence. This provides a proof of Donovan's Conjecture for resistant $2$-generated $2$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Pete Gautam

item.title: Newforms as test vectors for representations of Saito-Kurokawa type
item.description: arXiv:2611.15483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study irreducible (admissible) representations $\pi$ of the split group $G_n=SO(2n+1)$, both over finite and $p$-adic fields, which are distinguished for the (unramified) nonsplit form of $K_n=SO(2n)$ and for one more subgroup $H_n$. Over finite fields, $H_n$ is the split $SO(2n)$ while over $p$-adic fields it is the Gross-Tsai paramodular subgroup (of minimal level for $\pi$). These are all multiplicity one situations. With $0 \neq \ell_{n,K} \in {\rm Hom}_{K_n}(\pi_n,1)$ and $0 \neq v_{n,H} \in \pi_n^{H_n}$, both being one dimensional spaces, we are interested in the vanishing/nonvanishing of $|\ell_{n,K}(v_{n,H})|^2$. Appropriately normalized, this defines the notion of the correlation coefficient $c(\pi;H_n,K_n)$ of $H_n$ and $K_n$ in $G_n$ with respect to $\pi$. Via the theta correspondence between ${\rm SL}(2)$ (or ${\rm Mp}(2)$), we establish a bijection $\pi_n \leftrightarrow \pi_1$ between representations of $G_n$ and $G_1$ under consideration. Our main results then prove that $d_n c(\pi_n;H_n,K_n)$ is independent of the rank $n$, where $d_n =\dim \pi_n$ for finite fields and is defined in terms of the index of $H_n$ in the standard maximal compact subgroup of $G_n$ in the $p$-adic case. We also highlight a conjecture from [Ana25] on Legendre polynomials modulo $p$. Its truth will have the arithmetic consequence that over $\mathbb F_p$, given $\pi_1$, we can choose $u \in \mathbb F_p$ such that, in every rank $n$, all the correlation coefficients $c(\pi_n;H_n,u_nK_n u_n^{-1})$ are simultaneously nonzero and moreover they belong to $\mathbb Z_p^\times$ under any identification $\mathbb C \simeq \overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, where $u_n$ is a specific unipotent element in $G_n$ corresponding to $u$.
item.dc:creator: U. K. Anandavardhanan

item.title: Lax Centers and Monoidal Functors for Comodule Categories Associated with Acyclic Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.15496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the monoidal category of finite-dimensional right comodules over the path algebra $\Bbbk Q$ of a finite acyclic quiver $Q$, equipped with the weak bialgebra structure in which every path is grouplike. We prove that the lax center of this category is monoidally equivalent to $\operatorname{Rep}^{\mathrm{fd}}_{\Bbbk}(Q)$, the category of finite-dimensional representations of $Q$. We also classify all $\Bbbk$-linear strong monoidal functors between any two such comodule categories, and all monoidal natural transformations between them. For the right adjoint of such a functor, we determine when the left or right projection formula holds. When both projection formulas hold, this adjoint will induce a functor between the lax centers, and we describe the induced functor explicitly on quiver representations.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Zhao, Jingheng Zhou

item.title: Specializations of frozen variables for Grassmannian cluster algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.15611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The homogeneous coordinate ring of a Grassmannian variety $\mathrm{Gr}_{k,n}$ is equipped with a structure of a cluster algebra. The frozen variables are identified with the Pl\"ucker coordinates corresponding to length-$k$ segments of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. We study two families of algebras: the first family is obtained by specializing all the frozen variables and the second corresponds to the specialization of the nonwrapping variables. We construct flat bases in both families and study their affine spectra. The special fibers of the families are cones over projective varieties. We identify the irreducible components of these projective varieties with certain positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Jian-Rong Li

item.title: Affine Grassmannian from divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.15788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize Mirkovi\'c's construction of Zastava spaces. These spaces form an inductive system, giving a generalization of affine and Beilinson--Drinfeld Grassmannians as indschemes, defined for any integral symmetric matrix $\kappa$ with even diagonal entries. When $\kappa$ is the Cartan matrix from a simply-laced Kac--Moody algebra, we also construct an action of the Tits group on the generalized affine Grassmannian.
item.dc:creator: Chunlin Shao

item.title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
item.description: arXiv:2611.16002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.
item.dc:creator: Yvann Gaudillot-Estrada

item.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.16014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Brou\'e--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Eteve

item.title: On the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.16017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Brou\'e--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Eteve

item.title: Non-counital Frobenius algebras and QF-3 algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.16024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that non-counital Frobenius algebras with injective comultiplication coincide with QF-3 algebras, thereby providing a new characterization of QF-3 algebras. As an application, we recover that gendo-Frobenius algebras, self-injective algebras, and more generally Morita algebras, all admit an injective non-counital Frobenius algebra structure. Furthermore, we construct a canonical family of injective comultiplications on QF-3 algebras that admit a counit if and only if the algebra is Frobenius. This settles a question of Hernandez--Walton--Yadav and unifies a wealth of results in the literature. We conclude with applications to topological quantum field theories and Poincar\'e duality algebras.
item.dc:creator: Pablo S. Ocal

item.title: Tautological generation of preprojective BPS cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.16036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q$ be a quiver and let $\mathbf{d}$ be a dimension vector. We prove that the affinized BPS cohomology of the stack of $\mathbf{d}$-dimensional representations of the preprojective algebra $\Pi_Q$ is generated by its reduced virtual fundamental class under the action of tautological classes. This is a generalisation to singular quiver varieties of the Kirwan surjectivity statement of McGerty-Nevins for smooth framed quiver varieties. We prove that the statement holds for every King stability condition. To prove this, we attach legs to vertices of $Q$ and construct a correspondence with a smooth quiver variety for the extended quiver. This correspondence sends the reduced virtual fundamental class of the singular preprojective quiver stack to the Vandermonde determinant capped with the fundamental class of the smooth preprojective quiver stack for the leg-extended quiver. We construct the Weyl group action by the simultaneous Springer resolution of Dobrovolska-Ginzburg-Travkin, providing a comparison of the cohomology of fibres. This comparison preserves the tautological Chern classes. The sign-isotypic formula involving Kac polynomials of Hausel-Letellier-Rodriguez-Villegas, combined with Kirwan surjectivity for smooth framed quiver varieties of McGerty-Nevins, then implies the tautological generation theorem. We also describe the sign isotypic component of the cohomology of quiver varieties using the real-root subalgebras of the BPS Lie algebra. The tautological generation result can be extended via similar methods to deformed preprojective algebras of Crawley-Boevey-Holland at central parameters.
item.dc:creator: Ben Davison, Lucien Hennecart

item.title: Auslander-Reiten relations and local finiteness in extriangulated categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.16277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Hom-finite Krull--Schmidt extriangulated category over a commutative artin ring. Write ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup of the split Grothendieck group generated by the relations of all $\mathbb E$-triangles, and ${\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$ for the subgroup generated by those coming from Auslander--Reiten $\mathbb E$-triangles. We first prove that either one-sided finiteness condition on Hom supports implies ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. For incoming Hom supports, the proof uses a Jordan--H\"{o}lder filtration of the contravariant defect. The outgoing case follows by duality. This gives a new proof of the implication from local finiteness to generation by Auslander--Reiten relations. Our argument uses defects and induction on their composition length. In this way, it avoids the radical filtration argument used by Zhu and Zhuang. We then sssume that $\mathcal C$ has enough projectives and injectives, and prove that $\mathcal C$ is locally finite if and only if its projective and injective subcategories are locally finite, the Euler functions associated with Auslander--Reiten relations have finite support, stable and costable morphisms detect ordinary morphisms away from the projective and injective boundary, and ${\rm Rel}(\mathcal C)={\rm AR}(\mathcal C)$. Our results recover the classical module and triangulated cases. They also explain why the two one-sided support conditions are equivalent in the triangulated setting, but may differ in a general extriangulated category.
item.dc:creator: Panyue Zhou, Bin Zhu

item.title: Grothendieck groups and Auslander--Reiten relations in extended module categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.16343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider Grothendieck groups of extended module categories $\C_m(A)=m\text{-}\modu A$, where $A$ is a finite-dimensional algebra over a field and $m$ is a positive integer. We show that the relation subgroup of the split Grothendieck group of $\C_m(A)$ is generated by Auslander--Reiten extriangles if and only if $\C_m(A)$ has finitely many indecomposable objects up to isomorphism. To this end, we establish a criterion for extriangulated categories with bounded negative extension sequences and a finite extension generator. We then apply this criterion to extended module categories and recover the two-term silting criterion of Padrol, Palu, Pilaud and Plamondon. We also use the cohomological Euler characteristic to determine the rank of the relation subgroup. In particular, when $A$ is hereditary and representation-finite, we explicitly describe the indecomposable objects of $\C_m(A)$ and calculate the rank of its relation subgroup.
item.dc:creator: Yajie Xiang, Xiao Zhuang

item.title: Continuous representations of topological monoids via reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.16436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous representations of topological monoids on discrete modules via a finite-restriction reconstruction method. For an arbitrary topological monoid $\mathscr{M}$, we construct a transformation monoid $\mathscr{E}_\mathscr{M}$ whose uniformly continuous representations are equivalent to continuous representations of $\mathscr{M}$ on discrete modules. By the finite-restriction reconstruction, these categories are equivalent to categories of sheaves of modules over special sites. We illustrate this method by several examples, including various realizations of $\mathrm{FA}$-modules and continuous representations of $\operatorname{End}_A(\varinjlim_r A^r)$ for a finite ring $A$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxing Di, Liping Li, Li Liang

item.title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.16453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.
item.dc:creator: Linfang Hou, Si Li, Yongchang Zhu

item.title: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
item.description: arXiv:2611.16847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Xuhua He

item.title: Critical schemes, jet syzygies, and twisted periods
item.description: arXiv:2611.14631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study nonreduced critical schemes with prescribed support on nilpotent orbit closures and on the Kleinian singularity $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, and show that one specified minimal invariant syzygy among the first jet equations fixes their scheme structure. For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_N$ or $\mathfrak{so}_{2N}$ with Coxeter number $h$ and $p\ge2$ coprime to $h$, the selected polynomial is the coefficient of $s^{p+1}$ in $\det(1-sM)^{p/h}$, with reduced critical locus $\{M^p=0\}$, and the selecting syzygy is equivalent to the twisted period equation of Dubrovin and Feigin-Silantyev. The minimal invariant syzygies of that degree correspond to the lowest nonquadratic twisted periods, which, for $\mathfrak{so}_8$, form the standard representation of triality; in type D the Betti number alone does not determine the scheme. On $\mathbb C^2/\mathbb Z_n$, the selected polynomial is given by a terminating hypergeometric series. Restriction to Slodowy slices commutes with forming critical schemes and their nilradicals. These results determine, uniformly in rank and degree, the rings and nilradical filtrations through which the Schur and Macdonald indices of the corresponding Argyres-Douglas theories are proposed to arise as Hilbert series of arc spaces.
item.dc:creator: Monica Jinwoo Kang

item.title: On Tunnel Fusion and Yangian $R$-matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.14793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: XXX spin-chain Hamiltonians can be derived within the $R$-matrix formalism. For a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, the rational $R$-matrix $R$ intertwines the coproduct $\Delta$ in the Yangian $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{g})$. $R$ admits a particular Gauss decomposition $R=LDU$, where the upper-triangular matrix $U$ can be obtained from the lower-triangular matrix $L$. We treat $U$ in three ways. Algebraically, $U$ is known as a factorization twist. It plays the role of a ``universalizer'': it conjugates a non-universal pseudo-coproduct $\mathscr{D}$ in the molten crystal chain basis to the true Yangian coproduct $\Delta=U^{-1}\mathscr{D} U$. Physically, $U$ can be obtained as a Berry phase in SUSY quiver QFT for a quiver associated with the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this case, $U$ is calculated as a sum over tunneling amplitudes. Geometrically, $U$ can be interpreted as a renormalized Maulik-Okounkov stable envelope localized at a fixed point. In the physical setting, the Yang-Baxter equation (YBE), which ensures integrability, follows from the flatness of the Berry connection, which in turn follows from supersymmetry. However, the YBE imposes subtle constraints on the tunneling amplitudes, which we examine here. We construct recursion relations that allow higher collective amplitudes to be obtained from more elementary ones. We observe that different tunneling channels are in fact intertwined, leading to finer cancellations among amplitudes and to wall-crossing phenomena: depending on the parameters, the same amplitude is represented as a sum over different channels. We focus on $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ with higher-spin and non-evaluation representations, as well as on the fundamental representation of $\mathsf{Y}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1})$.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Galakhov

item.title: Automating the Derivation of Advanced Algorithms in Numerical Linear Algebra using Associative Algebras with Involution
item.description: arXiv:2611.14831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard algorithms of numerical linear algebra use their scalars through seven operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the adjoint, the $*$-square root and $(i,j)$ indexing. This thesis overloads these operations, as automatic differentiation overloads arithmetic, allowing scalars in associative algebras with involution. Many of the resulting decompositions and algorithms reduce to Hermitian eigendecomposition over these $*$-algebras. The decompositions are organised by doubly-signed quivers, whose vertices record real, complex or quaternionic scalars and the action of the involution. We prove an analogue of Gabriel's theorem: every finite-dimensional real $*$-algebra is a matrix algebra, with sizes and signs, over a quotient of its quiver's path $*$-algebra. Spectral theorems, the singular value decomposition, Takagi factorisation, Sylvester's law of inertia and the real Jordan form arise as unitary similarity problems for Hermitian matrices. Division and square roots take place in a completed localisation which inverts the arrows. For the singular value decomposition, Householder tridiagonalisation becomes Golub--Kahan bidiagonalisation. Over split-complex numbers, the QR algorithm becomes Rutishauser's LR algorithm, two steps at a time, and Cholesky factorisation becomes Doolittle's LU factorisation. These identifications require suitable $*$-square roots and hold whenever the steps are defined. Infinitesimals make limits of algorithms exact computations: Gram--Schmidt yields the Bruhat decomposition, and Gaussian elimination with pivots chosen by orders of magnitude yields Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm in leading terms. A Python library implements the seven operations and algorithms. An appendix visualises the QR algorithm on $2\times2$ real matrices.
item.dc:creator: Ran Gutin

item.title: Connection-twisted modules and logarithmic twisted modules of vertex algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the notion of connection-twisted modules for $\mathbb{C}$-graded vertex algebras, as suggested by Feigin and Lentner, and investigate their fundamental properties. Let $G$ be an algebraic group acting on a vertex algebra $V$ by automorphisms. We establish an equivalence between the category of $\nabla$-twisted $V$-modules and the category of $g$-twisted $V$-modules, where $\nabla$ is a regular singular $\mathfrak{g}$-connection and $g\in G$ is its monodromy. For symplectic fermion and affine vertex algebras, we explicitly compute the commutation relations and the action of the Virasoro algebra on connection-twisted modules, recovering the formulas obtained by Feigin and Lentner \cite{FL24,FL25}.
item.dc:creator: Takumi Iwane

item.title: Categorical orbifold theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.15630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the orbifold theory for condensable algebras in fusion categories $\mathcal{C}$. We prove that the algebra automorphism group of a condensable algebra $A$ is finite and explicitly characterize its elements in terms of the fusion action and indecomposable $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$-bimodule decomposition of $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. We further show that a finite group action on $A$ gives rise to a group extension of the category $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$ in $\mathcal{C}_{A}$. Conversely, every such group extension arises from a finite group of algebra automorphisms of $A$. Finally, we also construct a canonical maximal group extension of $\mathcal{C}_{A}^0$, thereby providing a categorical framework for the classical correspondence among finite group actions, fixed-point algebras, and twisted modules.
item.dc:creator: Chongying Dong, Siu-Hung Ng, Li Ren, Feng Xu

item.title: Dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.15830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the Artin--Schelter Gorenstein and Artin--Schelter regular properties descend from a graded Ore extension to its coefficient algebra, for every twisting automorphism and every skew derivation. We then determine the dual reflection groups of graded Ore extensions for all gradings compatible with the Ore structure. They are exactly the semidirect products of a dual reflection group of the coefficient algebra by the cyclic group generated by the degree of the new variable, meeting it trivially, and a nonzero skew derivation never contributes a new degree. For iterated Ore extensions we characterize the dual reflection groups by an order formula analogous to the theorem of Shephard, Todd and Chevalley, and we prove the binomial conjecture of Buzaglo and Rogalski for these algebras. We show that their covariant rings are complete intersections of growth type, whose Ext-algebras grow like a polynomial ring in as many variables as there are generators of nontrivial degree. This answers a question of Kirkman, Kuzmanovich and Zhang for these algebras. Finally, we describe the smash product as a Cayley quiver with relations, factor its matrix Hilbert series, and show that the extension becomes Hopf--Galois once the Jacobian is inverted.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Ait Mohamed, Asmae El-Baz

item.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.15962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Boixeda Alvarez, Do Kien Hoang

item.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
item.description: arXiv:2611.16105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.
item.dc:creator: I. Kotikov, P. Antonenko

item.title: The spectrum of free projective geometries over finite chain rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.16443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak{p}$ a prime ideal of residue order $q$, and $\mathcal{O}_r=\mathcal{O}/\mathfrak{p}^r$ which is a finite chain ring; the motivating example is $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$. The free projective geometry $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{fr}(\mathcal{O}_r)$ is the graph whose vertices are the nontrivial free submodules of $\mathcal{O}_r^{d}$, two of them adjacent when one strictly contains the other. For every $d$, $q$ and $r$ we reduce its adjacency matrix to explicit symmetric matrices (blocks) of size at most $d-1$. There is one block for each signature (a partition with at most $d/2$ parts, each at most $r$) and we show that every block, at every depth, is a single universal matrix $L(s,\sigma)$ evaluated at the number $s$ of parts of the signature $\lambda$ and at $\sigma=2rs-|\lambda|$. The same blocks give the spectrum of the subgraph induced on any set of levels, and for two levels this spectrum is completely explicit. All of it depends on the ring only through $q$ and $r$; in particular the subgraphs $\mathbb{P}^{d-1}_{S}$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^r$ and over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]/(t^r)$ are isospectral for all $\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\dots,d-1\}$; together with known rigidity results of arXiv:2510.09324, this proves that they are isospectral and non-isomorphic whenever $S$ contains at least two levels, as conjectured there.
item.dc:creator: Yishai Lavi

item.title: Matrix Waring Problem in finite fields with coefficients from $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.16651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer and $p$ be an odd prime such that $\gcd(p-1,k)=1$. For sufficiently large primes $p$, we show that the equation $AX^k+BY^k=C$ has solutions $X,Y \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $A$ and $B$ are fixed matrices in $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and $C$ is a fixed matrix in $\mathrm{M}(2,\mathbb{F}_p).$ Our proof relies on Fourier analysis over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{F}_p).$
item.dc:creator: Sutirtha Datta, Sourav Ghosh, Aniruddha Maji, Antara Manik

item.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.16837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Knesel, Petr Somberg

item.title: Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.16899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson

item.title: Poincar\'e polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.17014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincar\'e polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.
item.dc:creator: Marco Aldi, Samuel Bevins, Eleftherios Chatzitheodoridis, Sergio Da Silva, Quincy Frias, Tom\'as Mej\'ia G\'omez

item.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{slip-spli}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.17132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Chen, Honghui Ding

item.title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.17138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $\tau$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra $\mathbf{U}^0\subset\mathbf{U}$. We show that $\mathbf{B}$ yields a topological realization of the quasi-split $\imath$quantum loop group $\mathbf{U}^\imath$ associated with $\tau$, in the presentation recently obtained by Lu-Pan, building on work of Chen-Lu-Pan-Ruan-Wang on $\imath$Hopf algebras. By pullback, this gives rise to a rational restriction functor on category O representations. For modules with rational weights and generic values of the spectral parameter, every $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-submodule of a restricted module is stable under the derived quantum loop algebra $\mathbf{U}'$. In particular, irreducibility is generically preserved under restriction for such modules. For $|q|\neq1$ and under explicit assumptions on the quantum Cartan matrix, we construct meromorphic abelian K-matrices whose tensor counterparts yield boundary $q$-characters for both $\mathbf{U}$-modules and $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-modules. Finally, we extend the coideal construction and Drinfeld coaction to shifted $\imath$quantum loop algebras with arbitrary coweight shifts, providing a new approach to $\imath$GKLO representations by restriction from ordinary shifted quantum loop algebras.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Appel, Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki, Bart Vlaar

item.title: Algebraic and geometric aspects of Demazure weaves
item.description: arXiv:2611.17155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These are notes to supplement my talks at the Current Developments in Mathematics Conference in 2026. They are an expository account of recent work in the study of braid varieties and their relation to low-dimensional contact and symplectic topology. A driving theme is the development and use of Demazure weaves to construct cluster algebra structures on the coordinate rings of such braid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Roger Casals

item.title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.17162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.
item.dc:creator: Anif N. Shikder, Ramit Dey, Jan Minac, Lyle E. Muller

item.title: Reductive group actions
item.description: arXiv:1604.01005v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study rationality properties of reductive group actions over fields k of characteristic zero. In doing so, we unify Luna's theory of spherical systems with the Borel-Tits theory of reductive groups. Specifically, for any reductive group action, we define a generalized Tits index; its main constituents are a root system and a generalization of the anisotropic kernel. For k-spherical varieties (i.e., those for which a minimal parabolic subgroup has an open orbit), we obtain explicit smooth completions of the set of rational points. Over local fields, this yields genuine compactifications that generalize the maximal Satake compactification of symmetric spaces. Our main tool is a k-version of the Local Structure Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Friedrich Knop, Bernhard Kr\"otz

item.title: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
item.description: arXiv:2007.00342v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute projective dimension of translated simple modules in the regular block of the BGG category $\mathcal{O}$ in terms of Kazhdan-Lusztig combinatorics. This allows us to determine which projectives can appear at the last step of a minimal projective resolution for a translated simple module, confirming a conjecture by Johan K{\aa}hrstr\"om. We also derive some inequalities, in terms of Lusztig's $\mathbf{a}$-function, for possible degrees in which the top (or socle) of a translated simple module can live. Finally, we relate Kostant's problem with decomposability and isomorphism of translated simple modules, addressing yet another conjecture by Johan K{\aa}hrstr\"om.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Mathematics Research Notices, Vol. 2023, No. 4, pp. 3329-3373
item.dc:creator: Hankyung Ko, Volodymyr Mazorchuk, Rafael Mr{\dj}en

item.title: Classification of the d-representation-finite symmetric k-algebras of finite representation type
item.description: arXiv:2103.15380v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a complete classification of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric Nakayama algebras and of all $d$-representation-finite trivial extensions of path algebras of quivers, over an arbitrary field. As a consequence we get a classification, up to Morita equivalence, of all $d$-representation-finite symmetric algebras of finite representation type over an algebraically closed field.
item.dc:creator: Erik Darp\"o, Tor Kringeland

item.title: Crystal Structure of Upper Cluster Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2309.08326v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct upper seminormal crystals on the $\mu$-supported tropical points of skew-symmetric cluster algebras from their exchange matrices. A generic potential provides an additive categorification in which boundary representations determine the Cartan matrices and generic ranks describe the crystal operators. Under frozen-Jacobi-finiteness and reachability, the raising operators lift to locally nilpotent derivations of the upper cluster algebra. For $\tau$-exact boundary pairs, these derivations give integrable actions of derived Kac--Moody algebras in characteristic zero. In particular, the associated Cartan matrices are positive semidefinite. When the generic characters form a basis, this basis is BK-biperfect and the $\tau$-exact crystals are normal. We also construct algebraic Tits actions and describe compatibly pointed biperfect bases through a coefficient graph. The theory is illustrated by classical and new examples.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Inequalities characterizing distinguished unipotent orbits
item.description: arXiv:2409.06006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove a new characterization of the distinguished unipotent orbits of a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. For classical groups we prove the characterization by a combinatorial computation, and for exceptional groups we check it with a computer. This characterization is needed in the theory of cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters in the article ``Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters'' of the first two authors.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Bertoloni Meli, Teruhisa Koshikawa, Jonathan Leake

item.title: Minimal W-algebras of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one
item.description: arXiv:2506.15605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $N \in\mathbb Z_{\geq 7}$ we show that the simple minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_N$ at level minus one is isomorphic to the even subalgebra of the tensor product of the simple affine vertex superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{1|2}$ at level $\frac{N-6}{2}$ with $N-4$ free fermions. In particular when $N$ is even this minimal $\mathcal{W}$-algebra is strongly rational as conjectured by Arakawa-Moreau.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Creutzig, Justine Fasquel, Vladimir Kovalchuk, Andrew R. Linshaw, Shigenori Nakatsuka

item.title: Quivers with Polynomial Identities
item.description: arXiv:2508.00662v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a topological characterization of quivers whose path algebra satisfies a polynomial identity. This class includes the oriented cycle and acyclic quivers and, in the latter case, we describe the associated T-ideal. We introduce a generalization of Arnold's A-graded algebras, which we call locally A-graded algebras, and prove that they are also PI. We give an example of a quiver algebra satisfying a polynomial identity, even if the path algebra of the quiver does not.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Javier De Loera Ch\'avez, Elena Pascucci

item.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
item.description: arXiv:2508.01527v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.
item.dc:creator: Gurbir Dhillon, Sergey Lysenko

item.title: On irreducible representations of conjugacy quandles
item.description: arXiv:2604.22078v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $G$ a finite group, one way to construct irreducible quandle representations over $\mathbb{C}$ of the conjugacy quandle $Conj(G)$ is by taking the product of an irreducible linear group representation of $G$ by what we call a quandle character of $Conj(G)$ (a quandle morphism into $\mathbb{C}^\times$ ). We show that these are all the irreducible quandle representations of $Conj(G)$ over $\mathbb{C}$ if and only if the Bogomolov multiplier $B_0(G)$ of $G$ is trivial. The Bogomolov multiplier is trivial for many classical groups, simple groups and with exceptions quasi-simple groups. We apply this to study the enveloping group of $Conj(G)$. If $G$ finite with trivial $B_0(G)$, we obtain that the enveloping group of $Conj(G)$ injects into $G\times \mathbb{Z}^{c_G}$ where $c_G$ is the number of the conjugacy classes of $G$. If moreover $G$ is perfect the injection is an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Maassarani

item.title: Non-equivalence of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants
item.description: arXiv:2608.19570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Suppose $p > 7$ is a prime number, and $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field of residual characteristic $p$ satisfying $F \neq \mathbb{Q}_p$. Generalizing results of Ghate--Le--Sheth, Le--Singh, and Huang, we show that any split, connected, reductive group $G$ over $F$ which is not a torus admits a smooth, irreducible, non-admissible mod $p$ representation. We use this to show that the functor of pro-$p$-Iwahori invariants does not induce an equivalence between the category of smooth mod $p$ $G$-representations generated by their pro-$p$-Iwahori invariant vectors and modules over the pro-$p$-Iwahori--Hecke algebra, contrary to what happens for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.
item.dc:creator: Karol Koziol

item.title: Tilting realizations of derived-equivalent matrix centralizer algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.21922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be a centralizer matrix algebra over an arbitrary field. We prove that a centralizer matrix algebra $B$ is derived equivalent to $A$ if and only if $B\simeq{\rm End}_A(T)^{\rm op}$ for some tilting $A$-module $T$ of projective dimension at most one. We classify the basic tilting $A$-modules and identify their poset with a product of right weak orders on symmetric groups. For a fixed primary block, mutations exchange adjacent entries of the gap word. The isomorphism classes of the resulting opposite endomorphism algebras are parametrized by left cosets of the stabilizer of this word. The quotient of its labeled mutation graph by the stabilizer action is a Schreier multigraph. We also characterize when the right weak-order orientation descends to the nonloop edges of this quotient.
item.dc:creator: Jiangsheng Hu, Xin Ma, Jinbi Zhang, Tiwei Zhao

item.title: Fence Posets, Good Gradings and Frobenius Maximal Parabolics
item.description: arXiv:2609.10869v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak L$ be a Frobenius maximal parabolic subalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. For any $F\in\mathfrak L^*$ for which the Kirillov form $B_F(x,y)=F([x,y])$ is non-degenerate, let $\widehat F$ denote the associated principal element. We prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak L$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $\frac12$. We also prove that the multiplicities of the eigenvalues of $\operatorname{ad}_{\widehat F}$ on $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ form a unimodal sequence symmetric about $0$. The proof relates the ranked meander associated to $\mathfrak L$ to the order ideals of a related fence poset through Panyushev reduction. The known unimodality of the rank polynomial of the fence poset implies that of the meander, which in turn determines a good grading of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ in the sense of Elashvili and Kac. We prove that this grading coincides with that induced by the principal element and that the pyramid associated to this grading may be filled in such a way that its good element $e$ lies in $\mathfrak L$. The two unimodality results then follow from the injectivity properties of $\operatorname{ad}_e$ coming from the good grading and the duality induced by the bilinear form $B_F$.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Giaquinto, John Irving, Aaron Lauve, Mitja Mastnak

item.title: Degenerations of chain complexes
item.description: arXiv:2609.28051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study degenerations of orbits in varieties of chain complexes of projective modules. We show that degenerations are characterized in terms of certain admissible short exact sequences in the exact category of complexes of projectives, analogously to work from Riedtmann and Zwara. We then extend our study to the homotopy category. In this context, complexes of projectives with a given $g$-vector form an ind-variety, and we prove that degenerations of orbits are characterized by the existence of certain distinguished triangles in the category. This links to the algebraic definition of degeneration for triangulated categories introduced by Jensen, Su and Zimmermann.
item.dc:creator: Judith Marquardt

item.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
item.description: arXiv:2610.09312v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Chen

item.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.
item.dc:creator: Robin van Haastrecht

item.title: The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.01608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.
item.dc:creator: Qianhu Zhou

item.title: Lusztig sheaves, local systems, and the extended Springer resolution
item.description: arXiv:2611.05629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Springer resolution of the nilpotent cone is used to give a geometric construction of the Springer correspondence by applying tools in the derived category of perverse sheaves, particularly the decomposition theorem. In this paper we continue earlier work of the authors on the extended Springer resolution, a map introduced by the first author that factors through the Springer resolution. Our first main result shows that applying the decomposition theorem to this map yields a sum of Lusztig sheaves in all Lie types, each corresponding to a triple of so-called minimal cuspidal datum. We also study the simple perverse sheaves that occur as summands of the resulting sheaf. Our second main result proves that every simple perverse sheaf corresponding to orbits that are Levi-regular must occur, generalizing earlier work in the type A setting to all Lie types.
item.dc:creator: William Graham, Martha Precup, Amber Russell

item.title: Annular webs and Guralnick's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09114v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using annular webs and Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients, we disprove Guralnick's absolute boundedness conjecture for first cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Differential equations for intertwining operators among untwisted and twisted modules
item.description: arXiv:2510.14860v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given any vertex operator algebra $ V $ with an automorphism $ g $, we derive a Jacobi identity for an intertwining operator $ \mathcal{Y} $ of type $ \left( \begin{smallmatrix} W_3\\ W_1 \, W_2 \end{smallmatrix}\right) $ when $ W_1 $ is an untwisted $ V $-module, and $ W_2 $ and $ W_3 $ are $ g $-twisted $ V $-modules. We say such an intertwining operator is of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type. Using the Jacobi identity, we obtain homogeneous linear differential equations satisfied by the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ when $ \mathcal{Y}_j $ are of $\left(\!\begin{smallmatrix} g\\ 1 \ g \end{smallmatrix}\!\right)$-type and the modules are $ C_1 $-cofinite and discretely graded. In the special case that $ V $ is an affine vertex operator algebra, we derive the ``twisted KZ equations" and show that its solutions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points when $ g $ has finite order. When $ V $ is general and $ g $ has finite order, we use the theory of regular singular points to prove that the multi-series $ \langle w_0, \mathcal{Y}_1(w_1,z_1) \cdots \mathcal{Y}_N(w_N,z_N) w_{N+1} \rangle $ converges absolutely to a multivalued analytic function when $ |z_1| > \cdots > |z_N| > 0 $ and analytically extends to the region $ z_i, z_i - z_j \neq 0 $. Furthermore, when $ N = 2 $, we show that these multivalued functions have regular singularities at certain prescribed points.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Tan

item.title: Higher representation infinite algebras and toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two
item.description: arXiv:2511.02641v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of and classify basic $d$-tilting bundles consisting of line bundles on d-dimensional smooth toric Fano stacks of Picard number one or two. A $d$-tilting bundle is a tilting bundle whose endomorphism algebra has global dimension at most $d$. The classification is motivated by dimer models, where internal perfect matchings give rise to $2$-representation infinite algebras. The algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$ introduced by Herschend, Iyama and Oppermann are higher-dimensional analogues in the simplex case. The same principle leads to a new class of algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. Upper sets provide a common framework for tilting bundles, toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs), and cuts of higher-dimensional dimer-type quivers. In the Picard-number-one case, the bundles are in bijection with non-trivial upper sets in the Picard group, and their endomorphism algebras are precisely $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}$. In the Picard-number-two case, a first upper set determines the ambient toric NCCR, and a second selects an internal cut of its quiver. This gives a complete classification of such $d$-tilting bundles and realizes their endomorphism algebras precisely as $d$-representation infinite algebras of type $\widetilde{A}\widetilde{A}$. The resulting geometric models give a combinatorial description of $d$-APR tilting modules and show that both classes of algebras are closed under $d$-APR tilts.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Cluster Geometry of Universal Schubert Polynomials I: Geometric Bases and Cluster Monomials
item.description: arXiv:2608.29125v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Fulton's universal Schubert polynomials through the cluster structure on the upper unitriangular group and representations of type $A$. The convex hull of the initial tropical vectors of standard-elementary monomials is unimodularly equivalent to a product of simplices, and right-regular multisegments index three integral geometric bases of the standard-elementary module. A recursive prefix-record condition characterizes those universal Schubert polynomials that are homogeneous under diagonal conjugation, coincide with the corresponding generic and dual canonical basis elements, and are extended cluster monomials. On this locus, cover forests give squarefree factorizations into cluster variables. Outside it, the initial Laurent expansion has a coefficient $-1$.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei
